Let $X$ and $Y$ be real vector spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be nonempty, and let $A:X\to Y$ be linear. Supply metrics $d_X$ on $X$ and $d_Y$ on $Y$; for a purely algebraic instance with no specified metrics, use the discrete metrics $d_X(x,x')=0$ if $x=x'$ and $1$ otherwise, and likewise on $Y$. These metrics require no compatibility with the vector operations, and no continuity of $A$ is assumed. The discrete triangle inequality holds because, if two endpoints differ, at least one of the two successive pairs differs. Give $U$ and its subsets their restricted metrics. Thus every pair of real vector spaces still admits this convention. The corresponding metric-space inverse-problem model has admissible truths $U$ and forward map $A|_U$. An **admissible constraint class** is a nonempty subset $C\subseteq U$; its constrained forward map is the restriction $A|_C:C\to Y$. The class $C$ is **identifiable for $A$** if $A|_C$ is injective, meaning $Ax=Ax'$ for $x,x'\in C$ implies $x=x'$. Define the difference set and kernel by

$$C-C:=\{x-x':x,x'\in C\},\qquad \ker A:=\{x\in X:Ax=0_Y\}.$$

Let $V$ and $W$ be vector spaces over the same field $F$. A function
$T:V\to W$ is **linear** when

$$T(au+bv)=aT(u)+bT(v)$$

for all $a,b\in F$ and $u,v\in V$. Such a function is a **linear map**, or
**linear transformation**.

For a linear map $T:V\to W$, its **kernel** and **image** are respectively

$$\ker T:=\{v\in V:T(v)=0_W\},\qquad \operatorname{im}T:=\{T(v):v\in V\}.$$

That both sets are linear subspaces, and that a trivial kernel characterises
injectivity, is proved in [[thm-linear-kernel-image-and-injectivity]].

derivations.claim: Suppose $A|_C$ is injective and take $v\in(C-C)\cap\ker A$. By [F1], write $v=x-x'$ with $x,x'\in C$. By [F2] and [F3], $Ax-Ax'=Av=0_Y$, so $Ax=Ax'$. Injectivity gives $x=x'$, hence $v=0$. Since $C$ is nonempty, choose $x\in C$; then $0=x-x\in C-C$. Linearity also gives $A(0_X)=A(0_X+0_X)=A(0_X)+A(0_X)$, hence $A(0_X)=0_Y$ and $0_X\in\ker A$. Therefore $(C-C)\cap\ker A=\{0\}$.

Conversely, suppose $(C-C)\cap\ker A=\{0\}$ and take $x,x'\in C$ with $Ax=Ax'$. Then $x-x'\in C-C$ by [F1], and $A(x-x')=Ax-Ax'=0_Y$ by [F2], so $x-x'\in\ker A$ by [F3]. Thus $x-x'=0$, hence $x=x'$. Therefore $A|_C$ is injective.

For a singleton C, C-C={0}; the intersection is {0} and the restricted map is injective. See step 1.1.

For integers $1\le p\le n$, define the real Stiefel constraint set

$$\operatorname{St}(n,p):=\{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}:X^{\mathsf T}X=I_p\}.$$

Equip $\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with the Frobenius inner product $\langle U,V\rangle_F=\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}V)$ and norm $\|U\|_F=\sqrt{\langle U,U\rangle_F}$. Let $H=\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, let $Y$ be a real Hilbert space, let $U\subseteq H$ be open and contain $\operatorname{St}(n,p)$, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable. Given data $y\in Y$, a reference matrix $X_{\rm ref}\in H$, and $\lambda\ge0$, define the residual and regularized objective by

$$r(X):=\|F(X)-y\|_Y,\qquad \Phi(X):=\tfrac12\|F(X)-y\|_Y^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|X-X_{\rm ref}\|_F^2.$$

Supply an ambient gradient oracle $G:U\to H$ satisfying $D\Phi(X)[Z]=\langle G(X),Z\rangle_F$ for every $X\in U$ and $Z\in H$, an initial frame $X_0\in\operatorname{St}(n,p)$, a residual tolerance $\tau\ge0$, a finite integer budget $K\ge0$, and a step schedule $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{K-1}$ with every $\alpha_k>0$. For a square matrix $M$, put $\operatorname{sym}(M):=(M+M^{\mathsf T})/2$. The tangent-projection and metric-dual calculation for this $C^1$ objective, well-definedness of every tangent polar call, and finite-budget feasibility are justified by the finite-budget return and feasibility lemma. No smoothness beyond $C^1$ is required. The procedure is:

1. Set the current frame to $X_0$ and the schedule index to $k=0$. If $r(X)\le\tau$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{target-met})$.
2. While $k<K$, compute $G(X)$ and the Stiefel gradient $g:=G(X)-X\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}G(X))$. If $g=0$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{stationary})$.
3. Set $\eta:=-\alpha_k g$ and form the polar-retracted candidate

   $$X_{\rm trial}:=(X+\eta)\bigl((X+\eta)^{\mathsf T}(X+\eta)\bigr)^{-1/2}.$$

4. Evaluate $\Phi(X_{\rm trial})$ and $r(X_{\rm trial})$. If $\Phi(X_{\rm trial})>\Phi(X)$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{objective-rejected})$. Otherwise accept $X_{\rm trial}$ as the current frame. If its residual is at most $\tau$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{target-met})$; otherwise increment $k$ by one and repeat the loop.
5. When $k=K$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{budget-exhausted})$.

This procedure is restricted to the stated finite-dimensional real Stiefel constraint and the displayed polar retraction. It gives no convergence, global-optimality, or noisy-data stability guarantee, and it makes no finite-precision claim. It does not apply to positivity constraints or other nonlinear manifolds without a separately specified compatible retraction and proof.

For $X\in\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, the tangent space and its Frobenius
orthogonal projection are
$$T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)=\{Z:X^{\mathsf T}Z+Z^{\mathsf T}X=0\},\qquad \Pi_X^{\rm St}(G)=G-X\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}G).$$
For $[X]\in\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$, its tangent vectors have unique horizontal
representatives $Z$ with $X^{\mathsf T}Z=0$, and the quotient-metric projection
of an ambient $G$ to this horizontal space is
$$\Pi_X^{\rm Gr}(G)=(I-XX^{\mathsf T})G.$$

On the full-column-rank domains of [[def-stiefel-qr-polar-retractions]], the
positive-diagonal QR and polar maps are smooth, take values in
$\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, fix $\eta=0$, and have differential
$D R_X(0)[\eta]=\eta$. Their induced Grassmann maps are independent of the
representative and have identity differential under the horizontal tangent
identification. Thus they are first-order retractions. This theorem makes no
second-order claim; in particular, the QR map need not be second order.

derivations.claim: For a current $X\in\operatorname{St}(n,p)$, put $M=X^{\mathsf T}G$. From [F1] and $X^{\mathsf T}X=I_p$, the projected gradient satisfies $X^{\mathsf T}g+g^{\mathsf T}X=M+M^{\mathsf T}-2\operatorname{sym}(M)=0$. Thus $g\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,p)$ by [F2], and multiplication by $-\alpha_k$ keeps $\eta$ tangent.

Put $S=\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}G)$, so $S^{\mathsf T}=S$. If $Z\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,p)$, then $A=X^{\mathsf T}Z$ is skew-symmetric by [F2]. Hence $\langle XS,Z\rangle_F=\operatorname{tr}(SA)=0$: transposing and cyclically reordering gives $\operatorname{tr}(SA)=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T})=-\operatorname{tr}(AS)=-\operatorname{tr}(SA)$. The derivative of the restriction on a tangent $Z$ is therefore $D\Phi(X)[Z]=\langle G,Z\rangle_F=\langle g,Z\rangle_F$. Together with step1.1 this makes $g$ its tangent metric-dual vector. It is unique, since two such tangent vectors differ by a tangent vector whose pairing with itself is zero. This uses only the supplied first derivative, so $C^1$ suffices.

The initial frame is in $\operatorname{St}(n,p)$ by the input condition. Whenever a current frame is in $\operatorname{St}(n,p)$, step1.1 makes the trial tangent. Then $(X+\eta)^{\mathsf T}(X+\eta)=I_p+\eta^{\mathsf T}\eta$, so for $v\ne0$ its quadratic form is $\|v\|_2^2+\|\eta v\|_2^2>0$. Thus $X+\eta$ has full column rank, the polar call is in the declared domain of [F3], and [F3] puts its candidate in $\operatorname{St}(n,p)\subset U$. In particular every subsequent objective, residual and oracle evaluation has an input in its supplied domain. An accepted candidate is the next current frame; a rejected candidate returns the previous frame. Hence every current frame and every possible returned frame remains in $\operatorname{St}(n,p)$ by finite induction.

The index begins at zero, increases by one after each accepted nonterminal trial, and the loop ends when $k=K$; every other branch returns immediately. Therefore at most $K$ trial evaluations occur. The procedure accepts only candidates with objective no greater than the current value, and its residual test labels an output target-met exactly when its residual is at most $\tau$; every other return branch follows a failed target test and has residual greater than $\tau$.
